meta.note: Dedup-lookup experiment. Pass 5 measured SQLite answering an absent-key dedup check in 746 us vs LMDB's 0.50 us and hypothesised the un-checkpointed WAL. Four experiments, in order: (1) wal_hypothesis - checkpointing every 8 batches holds the WAL at 0 bytes and the miss still costs 393-456 us vs 2.29 us on an empty store, so the WAL is NOT the cause; (2) cache_vs_mmap - cache_size=64MiB barely helps (809->731 us) but mmap_size=1GiB gives 4.3x (809->189 us); (3) bytes_vs_keys - holding key count fixed and shrinking values 5461x makes the miss 76x faster (200->2.62 us) while 50x MORE keys costs 1.3x, so cost follows payload bytes, not cardinality: WITHOUT ROWID stores the row inside the index, so a key search descends pages full of 256 KiB chunks; (4) split_index_fix - giving the hash its own index over a rowid table drops the miss to 3.33-3.92 us and ALSO speeds warm chunk reads 4.8x (166->34.6 us) and ingest 17%. Engine-vs-engine gaps reported in passes 1-5 for SQLite reads were therefore largely schema and mmap artifacts. Standalone runs; not comparable record-for-record with the sweep passes, but split-vs-plain is same-context.

extra.note: latency = time to reopen an existing populated bucket DB
rmtree models per-bucket-file cleanup; delete_all_keys models shared-DB tombstones, whose space is only returned by the subsequent compaction
shared-DB bucket clear = in-place key deletes; sharded equivalent is a file unlink (~0.1 ms, full reclaim)
